answer.origin: NVIDIA Corporation blog post dated 2026-07-01 (party statement by NVIDIA, which also quotes Sharon AI CEO James Manning, Firmus co-CEO Tim Rosenfield, and describes DSX AI factory projects). Covered company: NVDA.
answer.note: NVIDIA's own July 1, 2026 statement says it is introducing a business model in which AI clouds procure NVIDIA infrastructure and sell NVIDIA-powered cloud services to AI-native, enterprise and ISV customers, with economic alignment through a revenue-sharing and credit-support model. NVIDIA says it would earn both standard product revenue and a share of cloud revenue on supported capacity, which it describes as a recurring, usage-linked earnings stream. Conditional interpretation: if implemented at scale, this would add a second revenue layer to NVDA beyond hardware sales, tied to the usage of AI cloud capacity, and would make NVDA partly exposed to the cloud operators' utilization and credit risk through the credit-support component. The source gives no quantified revenue share, credit-support size, contract terms, signed agreements or timing for NVDA's revenue from this model. The only numeric figure is a Firmus DSX AI factory campus in Batam, Indonesia, stated as expected to scale to 360 megawatts and up to 170,000 NVIDIA GPUs; this is a project plan from a company statement, not evidence of NVIDIA orders, delivery dates or completion. Sharon AI and Firmus quotes and AI-native customer references (Baseten, Fireworks AI, Together AI) describe demand context and intended use, not disclosed purchase amounts or commitments to NVIDIA.
limitations: The revenue-sharing percentage, the scope of supported capacity and the credit-support amount or terms are not disclosed, so NVDA's economic contribution cannot be sized from this source.
No signing status, counterparties' contract terms or timing are disclosed for the partnership arrangements with AI clouds; the source describes a model and early activity, not executed agreements.
The Firmus 360 MW and 170,000 GPU figures are stated as expected scale of a campus with no disclosed completion date, financing status or NVIDIA purchase schedule.
Sharon AI's collaboration is described only by a quote; no quantities, capacity or NVIDIA revenue are disclosed.
Customer references to Baseten, Fireworks AI and Together AI describe their compute needs and are not evidence of purchases from NVIDIA or from the named AI clouds.
follow_up: Check NVIDIA's next 10-Q or 10-K for any disclosure of revenue-share, cloud partnership, or credit-support arrangements, including guarantees, receivables or commitments tied to AI cloud operators.
Check Firmus and Sharon AI announcements and filings for signed agreements with NVIDIA, capacity timing, financing and any stated NVIDIA purchase commitments.
Check whether NVIDIA's financial statements report any deferred or contingent revenue, guarantee liabilities or customer financing linked to these AI cloud partners after the announcement.
